summary.text: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only astronomical object known to harbor life.
It is the only planet in the Solar System with liquid water on its surface, and its ocean covers 70.8% of its crust.
A liquid outer core makes a magnetosphere that deflects most solar wind and cosmic radiation, and its atmosphere is mostly nitrogen and oxygen.

items.prompt: Many places on Earth swing between summer and winter. What causes seasons?

options.label: It moves much closer to the Sun in summer
The Moon's gravity changes the sunlight it gets
Its rotation axis is tilted relative to its orbit
Its orbit is a long, stretched oval

items.explain: The tilt of Earth's axis of rotation with respect to its orbital plane around the Sun produces seasons.

items.prompt: Water vapor and carbon dioxide in the air capture energy from sunlight. What does that make possible?

options.label: A surface temperature at which water stays liquid
A magnetic shield against the solar wind
A steady slow drift of tectonic plates
A tide that rises twice a day

items.explain: These gases capture the Sun's energy, keeping an average of 14.76 °C where water is liquid under normal pressure.

items.prompt: What does the Moon's gravity do for Earth?

options.label: It keeps Earth's outer core liquid
It pushes tectonic plates around
It speeds up Earth's rotation
It raises tides and steadies Earth's tilt

items.explain: The Moon's gravity helps stabilize Earth's axis, causes tides, and gradually slows Earth's rotation.

items.prompt: The same face of the Moon looks toward us night after night. Why?

options.label: The Moon is far too small to spin
Earth's gravity has locked the Moon's rotation to its orbit
The Sun's glare hides its far side
The Moon's magnetic field fixes it in place

items.explain: Earth's gravitational pull has made the Moon's rotation tidally locked, keeping the same near side facing Earth.

items.prompt: As life spread across the young Earth, what happened to the planet itself?

options.label: Life stayed in the ocean with no wider effect
Life changed its atmosphere and surface
Life stopped its crust from moving
Life slowed its spin around its axis

items.explain: Life spread globally and has been altering Earth's atmosphere and surface, leading to the Great Oxidation Event.

items.prompt: Lakes, rivers, groundwater and the air hold a lot of water. How much do the polar ice sheets hold in comparison?

options.label: More than all of those put together
Less than the lakes alone
About the same as the groundwater
Almost none, because ice is solid

items.explain: Large ice sheets at the polar deserts retain more water than groundwater, lakes, rivers and atmospheric water combined.
